title: Southern Catalpa: Old Catalpas You Can Visit
meta_description: None of these three catalpas grew straight: one leans on columns, one corkscrews, one twists. Three mapped, in Amsterdam, Breda and Milan.
intro: Not one of these three grew straight. Breda's leans so far out over the pond in Wilhelminapark that the municipality now props its lowest limbs on columns rather than lose them. Amsterdam's turns as it rises, a slow corkscrew that the national guide to the city's monumental trees names as the reason to stop and look. Milan's has spent about 136 years twisting behind a baroque fish pond in the Giardini della Guastalla, until arborists describe its trunk as closer to sculpture than to a shade tree. The species comes from a small pocket of the southeastern United States and is far commoner in European gardens than at home. Dutch gives it two names and both are literal: trompetboom for the speckled cream flowers in July, bonenboom for the long thin pods that follow.
